title: Design an Authoritative Online Chess Platform
prompt: Design a global real-time chess service with matchmaking, rated and timed two-player games, reconnection, move history, and spectators. A game must have one authoritative serial command owner; clients may retry or reconnect and cannot be trusted to report elapsed clock time. Cover durable moves, event fan-out, owner failover, idempotency, ordering scope, and operational limits.

response.placeholder: Define the game authority and clock contract before describing WebSockets. Explain the durable write boundary and reconnect path.
response.reference_answer:
## Authority and API
Matchmaking chooses compatible players by time control, region, and a widening rating window. Creating or joining a game returns a game ID and player role. A move carries a client idempotency key and expected game version; the server validates turn, legality, and version.

## Per-game serialization
Route every command for one game to a fenced owner shard. The owner derives clocks from server timestamps, appends the validated move and resulting clock state durably, updates a latest snapshot, and only then publishes the new version. There is no global ordering requirement. A lease epoch prevents a former owner from publishing after failover.

## Reconnect and failure
A reconnecting client receives a snapshot plus events after its cursor. Clocks continue while disconnected. Persist timeout decisions as delayed durable work, not only an in-memory timer. Replicas and an event log allow a new fenced owner to recover.

## Operations
Rate-limit commands and spectators separately, bound hot-game fan-out, paginate history, and measure move validation latency, owner failover, reconnect gaps, illegal moves, and clock disputes.

## Progressive Hints
1. One game needs serial order; the whole service does not.
2. Persist before broadcasting.
3. A client clock is display data, not authority.
